links.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT bariatric surgery recommendations with actual clinical decisions
links.effect: Concordance was 20.0% (Kappa 0.003) without context and 25.8% (Kappa 0.068) after exposure to 412 articles; concordance with clinical judgment remained low.
links.quote: Concordance improved modestly to 25.8 % (Kappa = 0.068; p = 0.29), with a significant shift in global distribution (p < 0.00001).

links.outcome: Reliability of LLM treatment recommendations for surgical decision-making
links.effect: ChatGPT's surgical technique recommendations agreed poorly with clinicians (20.0% and 25.8% concordance), so it was judged not reliable for autonomous surgical decision-making.
links.quote: While potentially useful as an educational tool, ChatGPT is not yet reliable for autonomous surgical decision-making.

unlisted_practices: Exposing ChatGPT to a corpus of open-access scientific articles (contextual training) to improve recommendations
